newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European stocks up but off highs at midday.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European stocks up but off highs at midday.

text.p: European stock markets were up but off their session highs at midday on Thursday, shrugging off Wall Street's drop overnight.
The dollar was steady after Germany's central bank left interest rates unchanged, as expected, at its biweekly council meeting.
In stocks, the blue-chip CAC-40 stock index continued to lead Europe's bourses higher, but was off its record high 2,895.05 made earlier.
Rhone-Poulenc shares helped lift the index as shares were suspended limit-up after the company said it was considering buying out the rest of U.S. unit Rhone Poulenc Rorer.
German shares also shook off Wall Street's 68-point loss overnight. The DAX broke a psychological barrier at 3,800 to score a record high of 3,827.52 in early trade.
Profit-taking emerged in late morning to knock the index off its peak, but dealers said they did not expect any heavy selling pressure to surface to push the DAX lower.

London's FTSE-100 index overcame opening weakness with help from strong oil stocks. Oil stocks gained in line with firmer crude prices after the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) agreed to commit to quotas and cut production until the end of the year.
"If you believe that, then oil prices look good for now and will continue to look good to the end of the year," said an oil sector salesperson.
The OPEC agreement sparked a sharp sell-off in U.S. stocks and bonds late on Wednesday because the agreement was seen keeping oil prices high, which could lead to a bout of inflation.
But the FTSE was expected to stay in a narrow range, with gains capped by jitters before the Labour government's first budget on July 2 and the next monetary meeting on July 10.
Labour's budget is expected to hold bad news for investors on current tax breaks on divdends, and tax changes are seen hitting the corporate sector more than the consumer.
But hopes Labour will offer a smaller-than-expected windfall tax boosted utility shares. National Power and PowerGen were among the group's leaders.
With few major U.S. indicators slated for Thursday, traders might begin preparing for the second-quarter earnings onslaught, starting on Monday.

U.S. analysts expected the Standard and Poor's 500 companies to report a 9.2-percent average rise in second-quarter operating profits, according to First Call. That compares with the first quarter's 15.1-percent jump.
Weekly jobless claims and May's help wanted index are among the U.S. data due on Thursday. A Reuters survey forecasts jobless claims to fall to 340,000 from the previous week's 347,000.
CURRENCIES AT 1120 GMT
The dollar was at 113.68 yen and 1.7273 marks, compared with 114.03 yen and 1.7243 marks in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1120 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 11.5 points at 4,651.50.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 10.73 points at 2,878.17.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 9.50 points at 3,808.01.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed $337.90 at 1030 GMT against $338.25 at Wednesday's close.
